blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Blood Relations questions test the ability to trace generational hierarchy and family linkages.
Using a structured Family Relations Table simplifies complex puzzle-based queries.
Syllogism questions rely on the basic Venn Diagram Method for determining logical validity.
Mastering both Blood Relations and Syllogism is vital for scoring high in the SBI reasoning paper.

Concept:

Blood relation questions test the ability to understand family relationships based on given information.

blocks.content:
In SSC, blood relation questions are:

• Direct

• Mostly one family at a time

• No complex puzzles

Method to Solve:

1. Identify the starting person

2. Move step-by-step

3. Draw a simple family tree if needed

4. Read the question carefully till the end

Solved Examples:



Example 1:

A is the father of B. B is the sister of C.

How is A related to C?

Logic:

A → father of B

B → sister of C

So A is also father of C

Answer: Father

Example 2:

P is the brother of Q. Q is the mother of R.

How is P related to R?

Logic:

P → brother of mother

So P is maternal uncle

Answer: Uncle

Practice Questions (Blood Relations):

Q1. A is the son of B. B is the sister of C.

How is C related to A?

A. Uncle

B. Aunt

C. Father

D. Mother



Q2. X is the father of Y. Y is the brother of Z.

How is X related to Z?

A. Father

B. Uncle

C. Brother

D. Grandfather



Q3. P is the sister of Q. Q is the father of R.

How is P related to R?

A. Mother

B. Aunt

C. Sister

D. Grandmother

items: Always determine gender carefully in Blood Relations; do not assume gender based solely on names.
In Syllogisms, ensure all standard Venn diagram overlapping cases are drawn to test 'Possibility' cases.
Watch out for 'Either-Or' complementary pair conclusions in Syllogism problems.

blocks.content:
Concept:

Syllogism tests the ability to draw logical conclusions from given statements.



In SSC, syllogism questions are:

• Basic

• Mostly definite conclusions

• Best solved using Venn diagrams



Standard Statements:

1)All A are B

2)Some A are B

3)No A is B
